cautions: Page14 defines score as gradient log likelihood and G as negative expected Hessian, but displays a leading negative G inverse score expansion. With these definitions use the positive A inverse score expansion; derive it from the score equation.
Page13 correctly derives the minimization-loss sign but is not the same sign convention as the page14 likelihood score.
Page14 broadly states efficiency relative to every consistent asymptotically normal GMM estimator without all regular estimator/model restrictions. The chapter does not adopt that universal claim.
Page8 refers to a quantile function as nonincreasing; increasing quantile ordering is the relevant convention. Sorted effects are excluded.
Uniqueness/concavity does not guarantee an unconstrained finite maximizer under separation. Explicit finite boundary cases are required.
The selected source provides a stacked-moment route for APE uncertainty; the chapter supplies the explicit empirical-X term and retains its cross covariance under misspecification.

metadata_and_scope.title: 14.385 Nonlinear Econometrics, Lecture1: Basic Overview of Some Principal Methods
metadata_and_scope.scope: Conditional/marginal likelihood distinction, censored mixed likelihood and the TypeII sample-selection observed-data factorization. The explicit bivariate-normal selected density and Mills mean are derived in the chapter; page14 leaves the details to homework.
cautions: Setting the unavailable outcome to zero is a storage convention; the unselected contribution is probability mass, not an observed outcome density at zero.
The selected-outcome conditional density must be multiplied by the selection probability in the joint observed-data likelihood.
Distributional and identification hypotheses remain essential. The chapter does not import an unconditional efficiency or generic selection identification theorem.

metadata_and_scope.title: 18.650 Statistics for Applications, Chapter 3: Maximum Likelihood Estimation
metadata_and_scope.scope: KL definition and information inequality, likelihood maximization, gradient/Hessian, examples, information and regular limit statement. PDF page numbers differ from the slide footers by one.
cautions: Rendered PDF page9 has the correct not-equal/non-triangle signs that text extraction drops.

The page14 strict-concavity iff negative Hessian display is not a necessary condition for all strictly concave smooth functions and must exclude the zero direction. Use negative-definite Hessian as a sufficient condition on a convex domain.

The page15 score equation requires an interior attained optimum; strict concavity alone does not establish existence. The open Bernoulli/Poisson parameter spaces on pages17–18 also have zero-count/boundary existence exceptions.

Page24 explicitly leaves additional technical conditions unspecified. The chapter must supply compact measurable selection, uniform convergence, local Hessian and moment hypotheses rather than claim the slide gives a complete proof.

metadata_and_scope.title: Essentials of Count Data Regression
metadata_and_scope.scope: Poisson score/mean link and interpretation, overdispersion, selected/truncated count caution and Section4.1 correct-mean quasi-likelihood sandwich. The file name contains E01 but the document title page is dated June30,1999; no final publication year is invented.
cautions: Page3 concavity/iterative-solution statement needs sample rank and attained finite maximum; an all-zero count group can drive its fitted log mean toward negative infinity.
Page3 labels a derivative times one unit as a one-unit change. The chapter distinguishes an infinitesimal derivative from the exact finite exp(beta_j)-1 change.
Rendered page4 equation2.9 uses 1-F(c) for the stated event Y>=c; with F(y)=P(Y<=y) the integer endpoint should be 1-F(c-1). That censored-count formula is not adopted.

Rendered page10 contains a linear residual y-x prime beta in its omega discussion; use y-exp(x prime beta) in this mean model. The actual robust plug-in formula immediately below uses the fitted mean correctly.

Correct conditional mean alone supplies score centering, not all LLN/CLT, rank, existence or covariance regularity. The chapter proves those under explicit bounded-regressor and finite second-moment sufficient conditions.

evidence_limit: Scoped body and selected rendered equation inspection, not whole-document verification or acceptance. PDF bytes reused read-only; no new retrieval or external source introduced.
planned_scope: At most these four primary scopes; original KL/score/information/regular M-estimation arguments, binary separation/partial effects, correct-mean Poisson quasi-likelihood and honest observed-data selection likelihood. Reuse final c01–c03 proof interfaces rather than re-proving unrelated foundations. Distinguish functional form and sampling selection from causal identification.
proof_decisions: Use likelihood score s=gradient ell, A=-E Hessian and positive A inverse score influence; retain B=Var(s) separately unless information equality is proved.
Common-support dominated normalization derivatives prove mean-zero score/information identity; a moving-support uniform model deliberately violates interchange.

Compact measurable global selection and uniform criterion convergence give consistency before an integrated local Hessian obtains root-n rate; explicit bounded logit and mean-model Poisson primitives instantiate the theorem.

Same-sample APE influence contains h(X,beta)-tau plus G prime A inverse score. Correct conditional score centering removes the cross term; unconditional pseudo-score centering does not. A known fixed target distribution has no empirical-X term.

Selected-only density equals observed joint density divided by selection probability; derive the Gaussian formula by an orthogonal normal rotation and Mills mean by integration. No full selection-model identification or regularity theorem is claimed.
A logistic derivative evaluated at a discrete law is a model-dependent interpolation functional; no infinitesimal observed covariate variation or causal effect follows from that support.
